data.use_hpvc_sources: PV and grid power from HPVC

data_description.use_hpvc_sources: Use the PV and grid sensors chosen in HPVC, when HPVC has them (as in v2). Your own choice below is used otherwise.
data_description.pv_power_sensor: W or kW; kW is converted. Not needed when HPVC provides it.
data_description.grid_export_positive: Switch on when your grid sensor shows export as a positive value.
data_description.forecast_attribute: Attribute to read instead of the state; empty = use the state.
data_description.solar_today_sensor: Optional. Solcast (detailedForecast attribute) or Open-Meteo Solar Forecast (watts attribute).
data_description.irradiance_sensor: W/m², or a lux meter (lx is converted, about 120 lx per W/m²); needed when the weather station is used.
data_description.forecast_now_sensor: Optional. Leave empty when you have no solar forecast: HESC then plans on prices and charges on measured sun.
data_description.grid_power_l1_sensor: Optional, for the phase advice: the grid power of each phase from your meter (W or kW, net). HESC works out the sign itself.

data_description.ev_power_sensor: W or kW; kW is converted.
data_description.ev_soc_sensor: Recommended. Used for the charge goal, the minimum charge and 'car full'. Without it HESC plans in kWh only.

charger.title: Charger entities
charger.description: How HESC sees the charger's solar mode.

data_description.charger_eco_values: Comma separated mode values that mean the charger is in its solar mode.
data_description.charger_solar_switch_entity: Optional; only for chargers that also need a switch for solar charging.
data_description.charger_current_entity: Optional. Lets HESC turn the charger down while it charges from the grid, so more of the charge comes from the sun (the EV is still full on time). Wallbox: "Maximum charging current" (needs a Wallbox admin account).

no_solar_forecast.title: HESC works without a solar forecast
no_solar_forecast.description:
HESC now plans grid charging on prices only and charges on the sun it measures (PV power, or your irradiance / lux sensor). The charge plan counts no sun, so it never charges too late, and the kickstart is off.

With a solar forecast HESC plans smarter. Install one of these and choose its sensors in HESC's setup (Settings → Devices & services → HESC → Configure → Sources):
- **Solcast PV Forecast** (HACS, recommended): forecast now, in 30 minutes and today.
- **Open-Meteo Solar Forecast** (HACS): turn on its sensor "power production next 30 minutes".
- **Forecast.Solar** (built in): HESC reads its forecast series itself.

This note disappears once a forecast is chosen.

dashboard_url_taken.title: HESC dashboard not added: {url} is already in use
dashboard_url_taken.description:
HESC brings its own dashboard (sidebar: **HESC**, address {url}). Another dashboard already uses that address, probably one you made yourself by pasting HESC's YAML. HESC leaves that dashboard alone.

To use the dashboard that comes with HESC (it is updated together with HESC): delete your own dashboard under Settings → Dashboards, then reload HESC (Settings → Devices & services → HESC v3 → ⋮ → Reload) or restart Home Assistant. If the address comes from configuration.yaml or another integration, free it there.

To keep your own dashboard: ignore this notice.

set_charge_plan.name: Set charge plan
set_charge_plan.description: Sets the one-off charge plan (ready by, goal) and switches it on. For a Siri shortcut, a notification button or the Apple Watch.

day.name: Day
day.description: Ready on this day: Today, Tomorrow or Mon … Sun. Left out: the day already set.

time.name: Time
time.description: Ready at this time, a whole or half hour (for example 07:00). Left out: the time already set.

goal.name: Goal
goal.description: Battery level to reach: 50 to 100 %, in steps of 5. Left out: the goal already set.

charge_plan_off.name: Charge plan off
charge_plan_off.description: Switches the one-off charge plan off.

skip_plan_day.name: Skip a day of the repeating plan
skip_plan_day.description: The repeating plan does nothing on one day (a day off); the plan itself stays as it is. Without a date: the next day the plan would charge for.

date.name: Date
date.description: The day to skip. Left out: the next day of the repeating plan.

undo_skip_plan_day.name: Undo skipping a day
undo_skip_plan_day.description: The repeating plan charges again on the day that was skipped.

charge_now.name: Charge now
charge_now.description: Charges from the grid now until the EV reaches the goal, then the charger goes back to its own solar mode. Stops by itself when the EV is unplugged.

goal.name: Goal
goal.description: Battery level to reach: 50 to 100 %, in steps of 5.

charge_now_off.name: Stop charge now
charge_now_off.description: Stops "charge now"; the charger goes back to its own solar mode. A planned grid charge is not affected.

bad_plan_time.message: Time {time} is not possible: use a whole or half hour, for example 07:00 or 07:30.

not_loaded.message: HESC is not set up or not running.

no_repeating_day.message: The repeating plan is off or has no day set: there is no day to skip.

charge_now_shadow.message: Shadow mode is on: HESC v3 switches nothing, so it cannot charge now.

ev_not_connected.message: The EV is not plugged in.

no_battery_level.message: HESC does not know the EV battery level, so it cannot tell when the goal is reached.

charge_now_close.message: The EV is already at {soc}%: less than 3% below {goal}% or above it, so HESC does not start charging.

grid_not_set_up.message: Grid charging is not set up (a start/stop switch, or a mode entity with a 'charge now' value), so HESC cannot charge now.
